ONE DEFECT worth fixing, which did not stop the pass: assistantModel() in extensions.ts destructures `section('--settings--', '--help--').split('\n')` straight into [settings, config], but element 0 is the empty tail of the `echo --settings--` line, so settings is always '', the settings.json value is reported as coming from ~/.claude.json (the tooltip said "Read from `model` in the pod's ~/.claude.json" when the value was in ~/.claude/settings.json), and a model set only in ~/.claude.json is dropped entirely. Filter the empty leading line before destructuring.

The panel says so under the stream instead of inventing a number: "The per-step detail the design draws - a status and a duration for each step, and live progress on the one in flight - is not here, because the hooks record a turn's start, the files its editing tools touch and its end, and nothing in between." There are no step rows to expand: 0 .turn__step elements in the stream. Same cause as step-duration - no PreToolUse hook in the pod's settings.json, so no step is ever recorded. No step rows, so no step sub-line: .turn__step is 0. The per-turn file list the component can draw is a different thing and was empty here because no turn in this pod finishes (claude is not signed in). No PreToolUse hook exists, so a per-step file list has no source. Honestly absent.

So I recorded a failure for nodehealth instead, which does have a UIPlugin (v0.1.0), and opened /barn/editor/nodehealth: "Show the last working build" was drawn. Clicking it swapped the iframe from the pod's dev server proxy to /dashboard/home, the state chip to "Last working build · v0.1.0", and the explainer to "This is v0.1.0, not the build that failed - The frame is on this Rancher's own pages, where the version it is loading runs. That version is the last build of this extension that installed - the failed one never replaced it." "Back to the live preview" put the frame back on the pod. Both halves hold: the swap works, and the refusal on base is accurate rather than a dead button.

verdicts.defect: Driving it restores the whole working tree of barn-base-extension, which four other verifiers and the deliberate harness fixture (HARNESS.md, product.ts) are sitting in. There is no throwaway pod to drive it against, so the restore itself is unverified this wave. Needs a pod nobody else is using.

verdicts.evidence: Now drawn, which it was not last wave. With a failure recorded, [data-testid=barn-rollback-masthead] appears in the masthead between the snapshots clock and Undo, labelled "Roll back to the snapshot \"autosave 2255 on Aug 23\"" with the title "Taken 44 seconds ago. A snapshot is a point somebody chose, not necessarily a build that worked." It disappears again when no failure is recorded (v-if="failure && wayBack"). It resolves the same target and calls the same roll-back.ts module as the panel's button, so the two are one action rather than two implementations.
verdicts.defect: Not clicked, on instruction and for the same reason as the inline one: it restores the working tree of a pod several verifiers share. Presence, label and wiring are verified; the restore itself is not.

Minor wording nit: for an untracked file the undo removes it rather than restoring it, so "is back to its committed state" is not quite what happened; the effect is right.

There is no such button, and the panel says so where one would be: "There is no \"undo my request\" here. Nothing ties this failure to the request that caused it - the record holds the build's own output and no turn - and the per-turn file record the review screens read is blind to an edit made in the Terminal tab or through a shell command. Reversing \"the request\" would be reversing a guess. \"Undo the last change\" above is the honest neighbour." Refusing out loud is the right call; recorded not-implemented so the list stays honest about what the design asked for.
